memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the men got up to leave, they looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them on their way. Then the Lord said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?" - Gen 18:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something astonishing happens here. God pauses and asks Himself a question: "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?" And He decides not to. God chooses to take Abraham into His confidence, to share His plans, to treat him not as a distant subject but as a trusted friend.

This is a staggering privilege. The Creator of the universe deliberates over whether to confide in a human being - and chooses to. Abraham is being drawn into a closeness with God that goes beyond mere obedience into genuine friendship. Indeed, Scripture later calls Abraham "God's friend" (Jas 2:23).

Think about what friendship means. Friends share their hearts. They tell one another what they are thinking and planning. And here God treats Abraham as a friend, letting him in on what He is about to do. This is the kind of relationship God desires with His people - not cold servitude, but warm friendship.

Jesus made this friendship explicit to His disciples: "I no longer call you servants... Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you" (John 15:15). Through Christ, we too are invited into this astonishing closeness - friends of God, who shares His heart with us in His Word. Draw near to the God who wants to share His heart with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you relate to God as a distant master or as a trusted friend?
- Are you drawing near to hear God share His heart in His Word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, it amazes me that You would call me friend and share Your heart with me. Draw me into that closeness. Help me listen for Your voice in Your Word, and walk with You as a trusted friend.
Amen.
